message: Failed JWT decode falls back to jwt.decode with verify_signature=False and algorithms including 'none', letting any attacker forge a valid token for any user_id (full auth bypass)
JWT HMAC signing secret 'secret' hardcoded in source
Flask SECRET_KEY hardcoded to 'supersecret'
after_request reflects arbitrary Origin and sets Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true, enabling credentialed cross-origin API calls from any site
Flask app run with debug=True and host 0.0.0.0 — Werkzeug debugger allows arbitrary code execution
Seeded accounts use weak password 'password123'
SECRET_KEY=supersecret hardcoded in compose environment
username string-interpolated into INSERT SQL in /api/register
username string-interpolated into SELECT SQL in /api/login
Registration password hashed with unsalted MD5
Login JWT signed with hardcoded secret 'secret'
Session token cookie set with httponly=False and secure=False — readable/stealable via JS and sent over HTTP
/api/update-password takes arbitrary user_id from the body, allowing any authenticated user to reset any other user's password (account takeover)
Password reset token is deterministic md5(username) with no secret — anyone can compute it and reset any account
Reset token returned in API response as 'debug_token'
yaml.load with Loader=yaml.Loader parses untrusted user YAML — arbitrary Python object construction / RCE
User passwords stored as unsalted MD5 hashes (set_password/check_password)
user_id query param interpolated into raw SQL SELECT in /api/transactions
description search term interpolated into raw SQL LIKE in /api/transactions/search
/api/transactions/<id>/receipt has no authentication/authorization — any visitor can enumerate all transactions and user names
User-controlled transaction.description interpolated into unescaped raw HTML receipt page
/api/split-bill takes from_user_id from the request body and debits that user's balance — any authenticated user can drain any other user
transfer does not validate amount > 0 — negative amount inflates the sender's balance and drains the receiver
/api/quickpay performs no balance check (and no positive-amount check) — accounts can be overdrawn or inflated
Hardcoded production credentials: admin API key, AWS access/secret key, Stripe key, database password, SendGrid key, GitHub token
All /api/admin/* endpoints require only token_required with no admin role check — any authenticated user can invoke every admin function
report_type/date_range interpolated into shell=True subprocess.check_output in /api/admin/generate-report
service query param interpolated into os.popen(f'systemctl status {service}')
host field interpolated into 'ping -c 3 {host}' with shell=True
domain param interpolated into 'nslookup {domain}' with shell=True
requests.get on user-supplied URL in /api/admin/webhook-test with response body returned — SSRF to internal services and metadata
requests.get on user-supplied avatar_url with verify=False — SSRF plus TLS certificate verification disabled
filename param concatenated into /app/statements/ path and sent via send_file — arbitrary file read (e.g. ../../etc/passwd)
file param interpolated into /var/log/{log_file} and read — arbitrary file disclosure
lxml XMLParser(resolve_entities=True, no_network=False) parses untrusted XML — XXE file disclosure / SSRF (billion-laughs DoS)
pickle.loads on base64 user input in /api/admin/import-session — remote code execution
PUT /api/admin/users/<id> applies every JSON key via setattr — setting role=admin (or balance/password_hash) escalates privileges
render_template_string with user-supplied template string — SSTI leading to RCE
Unauthenticated /api/redirect follows user-supplied url param — open redirect (phishing/token theft vector)
User-controlled action/details written directly into log lines — log forging/injection
GET /api/admin/users returns every user's password_hash and full profile (SSN, DOB, address) with no admin check
DELETE /api/admin/users/<id>/delete has no admin role check — any authenticated user can delete any account
User-supplied regex pattern compiled and matched server-side in /api/admin/search-users — ReDoS DoS
eval() on user-supplied expression in /api/admin/calculate — arbitrary code execution
exec() on user-supplied script in /api/admin/run-script — arbitrary code execution
User string compiled then exec()ed in /api/admin/format-data — arbitrary code execution
SHA-1 used as integrity check in /api/admin/verify-integrity
API tokens derived from MD5 of user seed — weak, guessable token generation
Hardcoded master password 'MasterAdmin@2024!' grants admin access in /api/admin/master-login
Authorization enforced with assert() — stripped under 'python -O' and raises 500 rather than denying access
User content written to predictable /tmp/report_<id>.csv and served back — race/privesc on shared /tmp and arbitrary content write
GET /api/admin/dashboard-data returns the admin API key and AWS access key in the JSON response
Unsanitized uploaded.filename joined to UPLOAD_DIR and used to create directories — '../' sequences write files outside the uploads directory
No filename/extension/content-type validation before saving — arbitrary file upload (e.g. HTML/SVG) that is later served to browsers
serve_upload uses <path:filename> + os.path.join with no canonicalization — arbitrary file read via /uploads/../../etc/passwd
Uploaded files served with guessed content-type (text/html) and no X-Content-Type-Options — uploaded HTML executes in the app origin
eval() on user-typed calculator expression in the browser
window 'message' handler evals event.data.payload with no event.origin validation — any page/iframe can execute arbitrary JS in the admin panel
URL ?notes= parameter rendered via dangerouslySetInnerHTML without sanitization — DOM XSS via crafted link
JWT payload decoded with atob() and used for user_id with no token validation/expiration check
